children: Japan’s industrial production rebounded by 2.2% M/M in September 2026, beating market forecasts of 1.3% and reversing a 2.4% decline in August to record its fastest growth since January amid recovering export demand.

Meanwhile, the labor market showed continued strength as the unemployment rate unexpectedly edged down to 2.4% from 2.5% in August, with total employment rising by 340K to a four-month high of 68.68M and the number of unemployed dropping by 100,000 to 1.67M.

Retail sales grew 2.3% Y/Y in September, marking the seventh consecutive month of expansion, backed by government cost-of-living relief, though easing from August's revised 2.9% gain to record the slowest annual growth in three months, alongside a 0.7% M/M contraction.
Leading price indicators for October showed core consumer prices in Tokyo’s central wards rising 2.6% Y/Y, matching expectations and marking the first deceleration in five months.
